characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Crossbeam instrument (XB 1540, Carl Zeiss SMT AG, Germany)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Short annealed 8Al steel develops planar dislocation configurations formed by Taylor lattice structures and highly dense dislocation walls (HDDWs) spaced between 100 and 200 nm; planar dislocation substructures are stable up to a true stress of 1.1 GPa.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Short annealed 8Al sample tensile deformed to 0.3 true strain; longitudinal section, observation direction perpendicular to tensile axis
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the dislocation substructure (planar configurations, Taylor lattice structures, highly dense dislocation walls)
characterization_methods.technique: Electron channeling contrast imaging (ECCI) using an EBSD-based set-up under controlled diffraction conditions

characterization_methods.key_findings: Heterogeneous distribution of intragranular nanosized precipitates with sizes between 2 and 5 nm in the short annealed 8Al steel.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Short annealed 8Al sample; thin foils prepared by electropolishing using 30% nitric acid in methanol at -30 °C and 10 V
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the precipitation state (size and distribution of κ-carbides)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Precipitates are κ-carbides containing an L0_1-type structure with a cube/cube orientation relationship with the austenite matrix.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the crystal structure and orientation relationship of the nanosized precipitates

characterization_methods.key_findings: Short annealed 8Al steel: YS = 540 MPa, UTS = 895 MPa, UE = 65%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; initial strain rate 5×10^-4 s^-1; cylindrical samples with gauges of 6 mm diameter and 40 mm length
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure mechanical properties (YS, UTS, UE) and study microstructural evolution as a function of strain
characterization_methods.technique: Uniaxial tensile testing (to failure and interrupted to different strain levels)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Detailed TEM observations of the dislocation configurations do not reveal dislocation–particle pinning events; the κ-carbides are considered weak obstacles and, due to their tiny size, are crystallographically sheared, producing a moderate yield-strength increment and planar dislocation substructures.

interfaces.interface_notes: In the short annealed 8Al state the κ-carbide/matrix interfaces result from heterogeneous intragranular precipitation of shearable nanosized κ-carbides.

phase_interfaces.coherence: cube/cube orientation relationship with the austenite matrix

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar slip; planar dislocation substructures formed by Taylor lattice structures and HDDWs are stable up to high stress levels (true stress of 1.1 GPa), with the enhancement of planar slip attributed to the nanosized and shearable κ-carbides.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Yield strength increment from κ-carbide precipitation: 2Al steel in solid solution YS = 420 MPa vs short annealed 8Al steel YS = 540 MPa (moderate increment attributed to nanosized shearable κ-carbides)
Strain hardening capacity: the short annealed 8Al steel exhibits greater hardening than the long annealed 8Al steel; both exhibit a single, fairly constant hardening regime (~2 GPa at early stages)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Material melted in an induction furnace under Ar atmosphere.

processing_steps.method: cast to round bars, 25 mm in diameter

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cast ingots reheated to 1200 °C for 30 min prior to hot rolling.
Hot-rolled to 75% thickness reduction at 1100 °C and water quenched.
Hot-rolled material solution-treated for 2 h at 1100 °C under Ar, then quenched in water. This is the parent process (proc_solution-1100c-2h) of the short annealing.
Short annealing treatment (450 °C/1 h) applied after solution treatment; defines this sample's state (8Al, 1 h/450 °C).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: longitudinal sections examined (observation direction perpendicular to tensile axis)
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical tensile samples with gauges of 6 mm diameter and 40 mm length

strain_hardening_rate.note: early stages of deformation; single, fairly constant hardening regime

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: engineering stress–strain curve for 8Al-450°C/1h (green curve in Figure 1); the 8Al curve is nearly linear after yielding, does not show a concave shape, indicating a single hardening regime

precipitates.coherency: cube/cube orientation relationship with the austenite matrix; weak obstacles, crystallographically sheared

defects.type: Planar dislocation substructure consisting of Taylor lattice structures and highly dense dislocation walls (HDDWs) lying on the primary slip system, with HDDW spacing between 100 and 200 nm

microstructure_list.region: grain interior (tensile deformed to 0.3 true strain)

structures.overall_structure: Austenitic (γ) matrix containing a heterogeneous distribution of intragranular nanosized shearable κ-carbides; upon tensile deformation the alloy develops planar dislocation substructures (Taylor lattice structures and highly dense dislocation walls) that remain stable to high stress levels, giving a single, nearly constant strain-hardening regime.

unmapped_findings: The short annealed 8Al steel (450 °C/1 h) exhibits a single hardening regime with a strain-hardening capacity at the early stages of deformation (~2 GPa) that is lower than that of the 2Al steels (~2.6 GPa), and its flow curve is nearly linear (no concave shape) after yielding, in contrast to the multiple-stage hardening behavior of the 2Al steel.

The enhancement of planar slip in the short annealed 8Al steel is attributed to the nanosized and shearable κ-carbides, an effect linked to the high Al content (8 wt.%) that strongly modifies the strain-hardening behavior of Fe–Mn–Al–C steels.
